blocking.title: Authenticated prune is a replay after legacy deletion, not the production mutation after planClosedEpochCleanup
blocking.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:3181-3212 calls maintenance.pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix only after an already-supplied issuanceReceipt and fails closed unless replay.deletedAuthorSequenceRange === null, so this owner cannot be the first deletion. planClosedEpochCleanup( is only in the comment at :3192-3193; the sole production definition remains packages/node/src/internal/closed-epoch-cleanup.ts:442 and is invoked from tests/fixtures/phase-6b/runtime-reclamation-contract.ts:508, whose receipts are still produced by prunePublishedPrefix at :337-338 and :468-469. Legacy prunePublishedPrefix keeps the range-local unlinked-entry gate (conformance.ts:404-413, browser-issuance-store.ts:766-778, node-issuance-store.ts:835-845) and still deletes on an absent/incomplete plan, other-epoch row, or pending row. Kernel catch at v3-live.ts:3210-3211 maps a later plan-gate throw to D109D_RUNTIME_NOT_READY after rows are already gone. Design TDD item 5 / RED case 13 and the crash-matrix row 'prune with an unlinked plan entry | refused' are therefore not met on the production path; mixed-epoch pending/published authenticated reclamation is reachable only via direct store tests.
blocking.required_action: Make pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix the compare-and-delete mutation that runs after a real planClosedEpochCleanup result (verified adoption, two rollback generations, availability, complete outbox classification, expected-head). Do not accept a prunePublishedPrefix receipt as deletion proof. Prove an incomplete plan cannot lose issued or outbox rows, and that mixed-epoch pending/published authenticated reclamation is reachable through that owner. Keep legacy prunePublishedPrefix unchanged for creator-trusted-v1.

blocking.title: Authenticated prune is a post-hoc replay, not the deleting mutation; the full-scope plan gate runs after deletion (delete-then-gate)
blocking.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:3184-3202 derives an expected prior watermark from receipts.issuance.deletedAuthorSequenceRange and calls maintenance.pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix, then requires replay.deletedAuthorSequenceRange === null (v3-live.ts:3203-3209) — the call is expected to delete nothing. The receipt is produced by legacy prunePublishedPrefix (tests/fixtures/phase-6b/runtime-reclamation-contract.ts:337,468), whose plan gate remains range-local (packages/storage-node/src/internal/node-issuance-store.ts:835-845: only entries with sourceSequence inside [from, through] refuse; entries outside the selected prefix are ignored) and which still enforces single-epoch/published-only (:875-880). Consequently a plan with an unlinked or manual-review entry outside the selected prefix does not stop the legacy deletion; the authenticated full-scope gate (settlementPlanPermitsAuthenticatedPruning, node-issuance-store.ts:795-801) fires only afterward on the replay, which then throws ISSUANCE_RETRY_REQUIRED mapped to D109D_RUNTIME_NOT_READY (v3-live.ts:3210-3212) with the rows already gone. This violates design.md 'pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix refuses any row referenced by an unlinked plan entry', crash-matrix row 'prune with an unlinked plan entry | refused', and the review requirement that the gate reject every unlinked non-expire entry anywhere before deleting. Governing plan (:98806) requires the method to BE the 'monotone CAS deletion across old epochs and pending/published rows'.
blocking.required_action: Make the authenticated method the mutation that performs the deletion on the receipt path: under settlementProfileFor(...) === 'v1', the cleanup/reclamation owner must call pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix to delete (and accept its non-null deletedAuthorSequenceRange), not replay a legacy prunePublishedPrefix receipt; the legacy pruner must not run first for settlement-profile scopes. Re-run focused/retained/isolated gates with the invocation test strengthened so it fails on the replay shape.

blocking.title: No production invocation exists and mixed-epoch pending/published reclamation is unreachable in production
blocking.evidence: reclaimInstalledV3Runtime (packages/node/src/internal/runtime-reclamation.ts:152) — the only route to reclaimV3RuntimeKernel — has zero production callers: repo-wide search finds references only in tests/phase-6b-runtime-reclamation-red.test.ts, tests/fixtures/phase-6b/runtime-reclamation-contract.ts, tests/fixtures/phase-6c/retained-heap-worker.ts and its own definition; creator-close.ts imports only the release-owner functions. No product path invokes prunePublishedPrefix either (confirmed by the prior audit quoted in .logs/d110c-0c1-plan-confirmation-617c3cfa and by search). Even if the kernel were called, the receipt facts it consumes are constrained by planClosedEpochCleanup's copiedIssuance (packages/node/src/internal/closed-epoch-cleanup.ts:416-420) to epoch === closedEpoch and publishState === 'published' only, so the authenticated method's mixed-epoch/pending capability can never be exercised by this path. The 'production invocation' RED/GREEN test (tests/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5b0d-reclamation-red.test.ts:300-304) is a source-substring check satisfied by the replay call. Design f5b0d requires 'its production invocation on every peer after durable checkpoint staging, verified adoption, rollback-generation retention, availability and expected-head checks'; the retained finding 'nothing prunes in production; recovery-scan cap fails with age: f5b0d' therefore remains unfixed — with the new 3*maxEpochVertices cap (v3-live.ts:4492) and no real pruning, rooms older than three epochs still hit an age-dependent recovery failure, merely postponed from one epoch to three.
blocking.required_action: Wire the authenticated deletion into the real closed-epoch cleanup execution path on every peer (or, if D109d caller wiring is genuinely a later slice's scope, obtain an explicit accepted-design amendment moving 'production invocation' out of f5b0d and record the deferral with an owner); prove reachability with a behavioral test, not a source-shape assertion.

blocking.title: Authenticated prune is a post-hoc no-op replay in production, never the deleting mutation
blocking.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:3194-3209. The only production call site derives every argument from the caller-supplied `receipts.issuance` (a `DurableIssuancePruningReceipt` that already records `deletedAuthorSequenceRange`), sets `expectedPrunedThroughAuthorSequence` to the pre-deletion watermark, and then rejects any real deletion: `replay.deletedAuthorSequenceRange !== null` returns `D109D_RECEIPT_MISMATCH`. Because the receipt's watermark already equals `throughAuthorSequence`, every backend takes the idempotent-replay early return (node-issuance-store.ts:809-816, browser-issuance-store.ts:738-744, conformance.ts:384-389) and deletes nothing. The mixed-epoch pending/published capability the slice was built for (the `!authenticatedSettled` skips at node-issuance-store.ts:875/878, browser-issuance-store.ts:799/802, conformance.ts:434/437) is therefore reachable only from tests. Worse, on the one path where the replay *would* delete (a receipt whose deletion did not persist), the deletion commits and the kernel then returns `D109D_RECEIPT_MISMATCH` after the irreversible mutation. The GREEN's own README:24-27 states the design intent has been inverted: it 'replays the authenticated operation only after the existing cleanup receipt path has established ... facts'. Design.md:329-337 and plan-v2:98806-98808 require this method to BE the compare-and-delete after the gates.
blocking.required_action: Make `pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix` the mutation that performs the deletion in the production path — i.e. call it with the pre-deletion watermark/lineage as the CAS input and let it produce the receipt — instead of replaying a receipt produced elsewhere. Remove the `deletedAuthorSequenceRange !== null` rejection, or reslice per design.md:552-561 if the ordering cannot be inverted.

blocking.title: The 'verified adoption' gates the call claims are never executed; the RED that pinned them is satisfied by a comment, and an incomplete plan can still lose rows
blocking.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:3192 is a comment: '// The receipt pair reaches this owner only after planClosedEpochCleanup(...) has'. That comment is the ONLY occurrence of `planClosedEpochCleanup` in all of packages/ outside its own definition at packages/node/src/internal/closed-epoch-cleanup.ts:442 — v3-live.ts does not import closed-epoch-cleanup, and repo-wide the planner has no production caller (only tests/ and tests/fixtures/). Its refusals D109A_ADOPTION_INVALID, D109A_ROLLBACK_INSUFFICIENT, D109A_REVISION_STALE, D109A_SNAPSHOT_MISSING and D109A_POLICY_UNSUPPORTED therefore never run. `d109dRegistrationBound` (v3-live.ts:2982-3011) binds epoch/scope/boundary/manifest/QC/head but is a different, narrower set. tests/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5b0d-reclamation-red.test.ts:303 pins this with `expect(source).toContain("planClosedEpochCleanup(")` over the whole file — a gate the GREEN closed by writing the comment; .logs/d110c-0c1f5b0d-green-1063feca/source-shape-check.log:35-36 records the comment itself as the 'cleanup and recovery owner' match. Consequently review item 4's proof obligation fails: the actual deletion is still `prunePublishedPrefix`, whose plan gate remains range-local (node-issuance-store.ts:835-845), so an absent plan, a null `fenceSequence`, a `manual-review` entry, or an unlinked entry outside [from,through] all permit deletion and watermark advance, and the new global gate only fires afterwards on rows that are already gone.
blocking.required_action: Either wire `planClosedEpochCleanup` into the production reclamation path so its adoption/rollback/revision/snapshot/availability refusals actually gate deletion, or drop the false comment and the string assertion. Replace the source-grep RED case with a behavioural test that fails when the gates are absent. Ensure the plan gate runs on the deleting call, not after it.
